To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an oxidative chemical vapor deposition process that can deposit thin, fouling-resistant, and conductive coatings that can potentially be applied to the self-cleaning of electrolysis-based separation membranes and the field of bioelectronic devices.

zwitterionic derivatives of intrinsically conducting polymers (ICP) synthesized via oxidative CVD are multifunctional, thin films that are fouling resistant and electrically conductive, which are important for applications such as self-cleaning separation membranes and bioelectronics.
we have synthesized a novel class of thin, conductive, and fouling-resistant polymeric films via oCVD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and potential applications of multifunctional fouling-resistant, thin, and conductive coatings.

the synthesis of thin, conductive, and fouling-resistant coatings that are suitable for applications in electrolysis-based self cleaning, bioelectronics, and other applications where a multifunctional surface coating is desired.
the synthesis of multifuctional fouling resistant and electrically conductive thin films that have the potential to be used in a variety of applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fouling-resistant and conductive surfaces have been successfully prepared by oCVD.
the fouling resistances and electrical conductivities of oCVD-derived PEDOT films can be tuned by adjusting the deposition conditions and the chemical structure of the monomer.

fouling-resistant and conductive surfaces can be synthesized by the oxidative chemical vapor deposition of zwitterionic poly(3,3’-ethylenethio-4,4’-dioxoethylenediothiophene)-co-(4-vinylbenzyltrimethylammonium) bromide (z-PEDOT-co-PVBTMA) films, and that their properties can be tuned by varying the ratio of zwitterionic monomer to PEDOT
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fouling resistance is achieved by a combination of surface hydrophilicity, surface charge, and surface topography.
the oCVD PEDOT films exhibit excellent fouling resistance and conductivity, and the oCVD process is a promising technique for the synthesis of multifuncitonal surfaces.
the fouling resistances and electrical conductivities of the oCVD films are comparable to those of the other surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oCVD of PEDOT derivatives can be used to produce fouling-resistant coatings with the additional property of electrical conductivity, which is necessary for applications in electrolysis-based self cleaning and in the field bioelectronics.
fouling-resistant coatings can be made conductive without compromising fouling resistance.
oCVD can be utilized to synthesize thin fouling-resistant and conductive films.
